title: Why you will NEVER have freaky, thick forearms if your wrists are small (Natty or not)
summary: NH reacts line by line to a Natty or Not article claiming forearm size is purely genetic: short muscle bellies, small wrists, tendons that do not grow. He argues that forearms grow with training, as welders and arm wrestlers show, that PEDs and diffuse tonnage explain untrained pro forearms, and that measurements beat the mirror. He uses his own 6-6.5 inch wrists and 18 inch arms as proof.
claims: Human potential is almost infinite: any muscle you want to grow will grow if you train it
Dreaming and high hopes are always better than a blackpill loser's mindset; if you do not believe in it, you will not work hard or progress
Deadlifts are a poor forearm builder; they are mostly a static grip hold
Short muscle bellies are not specific to forearms and calves, and a muscle on a short segment can still grow
A longer muscle belly gives more overall growth potential, but a short one still grows over its own length
Short muscle bellies pop more and look freakier, e.g. short biceps give a better peak
Blaming genetics is a way to avoid responsibility
Pros like Ronnie Coleman had big untrained forearms because of diffuse tonnage from PEDs; that does not apply to naturals
The biggest forearms he has seen were on welders; they cannot all have long attachments, so the common factor is constant gripping and wrist flexion
A long attachment makes an untrained muscle look smaller and stick-like; short-attachment muscles pop more in 3D, which matters in bodybuilding
Tendons grow, but less than muscle and with no visual effect
The bony area without muscle on the back of the arm is what creates the triceps horseshoe
Arm wrestlers have huge forearms, often matching upper-arm size (17 and 17 inches), because they do a ton of wrist flexion
Do not inject; a small guy before testosterone is only a slightly bigger small guy after
PEDs grow muscles with many androgen receptors, gifted parts and trained parts, but neglected parts stay small; many pros have poor calves and forearms because they do not train them
Arnold had poor calves and fixed them by training them every day for two years (implant rumors aside)
He has trained calves seriously for about eight months and they are growing; calves stay small because nobody trains them, as it is boring
Toning is not a thing: a muscle grows or it does not; looking toned means more muscle and less fat
Quads are the easiest body part to grow; if yours do not grow, you do not know how to train
High-rep routines that are all volume and no intensity will not make you grow
Training should be so central to your life that you would sooner lose your nails than stop; if you do not like training you will never get big
You cannot see muscle change after a few days; people typically notice change after 6-12 months even though measurements show growth after about 4 months
Measurements, not the mirror, are the only reliable way to know if a muscle grew; he measures every body part he specializes
After stopping training, fat often goes to the legs, which can hide muscle loss in leg measurements
Exceptionally long muscle bellies can look bad; long-attachment biceps can look like potatoes, and balance is what matters
He has short quad attachments (good quads), medium biceps attachments and short forearm attachments with naked wrists
Thicker bones push muscle further out and look bigger but are not directly correlated with bigger muscles, though a bigger frame carries more mass more easily
Being small-framed, he could not carry 240 lb; it was too heavy for him
Despite 6-6.5 inch wrists and small hands he built 18 inch pumped upper arms by never worrying about wrist size and just training curls and wrist flexions
His inner forearm has always been strong; the outer forearm is catching up
For forearms: focus on programming, do arm days and isolation, and be patient because they are small muscles that take time
exercises: high frequency, like welders and arm wrestlers
mostly isometric grip; not a forearm builder
